questions.question: Which of the following articles of the Indian constitution is related to "Uniform civil code for the citizen"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Article 44__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 44 - The State shall endeavour to secure for the citizens a uniform civil code throughout the territory of India.
 
• The Uniform Civil Code calls for the formulation of one law for India, which would be applicable to all religious communities in matters such as marriage, divorce, inheritance, adoption, etc.
 
 
• Dr. B R Ambedkar, while formulating the Constitution had said that a UCC is desirable but for the moment it should remain voluntary.
 
• It was incorporated in the Constitution as an aspect that would be fulfilled when the nation would be ready to accept it and the social acceptance of the UCC could be made.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• To provide early childhood care and education for all children until they complete the age of six years (Article 45).
 
• To organize agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines (Article 48).
 
• To protect and improve the environment and to safeguard forests and wildlife (Article 48 A).
 
• To protect monuments, places, and objects of artistic or historic interest that are declared to be of national importance (Article 49).
 
• To separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State (Article 50).
 
• To promote international peace and security and maintain just and honourable relations between nations; to foster respect for international law and treaty obligations, and to encourage settlement of international disputes by arbitration (Article 51).

questions.question: Which are the most widespread forests in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Tropical Deciduous Forests__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Tropical Deciduous Forests:

__
 
• They are the most widespread in India.
 
• They are also called monsoon forests.
 
• They spread over regions that receive rainfall between 70-200 cm.
 
• Based on the availability of water, these forests are further divided into moist and dry deciduous.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Tropical Evergreen Forests are found in warm and humid areas with annual precipitation of over 200 cm and a mean annual temperature above 22°C.
 
• Mountain forests can be defined as forests
 
 
• On land with an elevation of 2500 m above sea level or higher, irrespective of the slope, or
 
• On land with an elevation of 300–2500 m and a slope with sharp changes in elevation within a short distance.
 
 
 
• Mangrove forests are productive wetlands that occur in coastal intertidal zones.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of Millets or coarse grains?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wheat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Millets are Cereals that are called coarse grains.
 
• They have high nutritional value and protein.
 
• Examples- are jawar, bajra, ragi, and maize.
 
• Millets are examples of Kharif crops.
 
• Jowar, bajra, and ragi are important millets grown in India.
 
• Though these are known as coarse grains, they have very high nutritional value.
 
• Jowar is the third most important food crop with respect to area and production.

 
• 160th session of the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) Council, held in Rome in December 2018, approved India’s proposal to observe an International Year of Millets in 2023.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Types of Crops:
 
• Kharif Crops:
 
 
• The crops which are grown in the monsoon season are known as Kharif crops. 
 
• For eg., maize, millet, and cotton.
 
• The seeds are sown at the beginning of the monsoon season and harvested at the end of the monsoon season.
 
 
 
• Rabi Crops:
 
 
• The name “Rabi” means “spring” – a word derived from Arabic. 
 
• The crops that are grown in the winter season and harvested in the spring are called Rabi crops.
 
• Wheat, gram, and mustard are some of the Rabi crops.
 
• Various agricultural practices are carried out to produce new crop varieties.
 
 
 
• Zaid Crops:
 
 
• Such crops are grown between the Kharif and Rabi seasons, i.e., between March and June. 
 
• These crops mature early.
 
• Cucumber, pumpkin, bitter gourd, and watermelon are zaid crops.

questions.question: In Table Tennis, the length of upper surface of the table is _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**274 cm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The upper surface of the table, known as the playing surface, is **2.74 m or 274 cm long** and 1.525m wide and is horizontal 76cm above the floor. 
 
• The playing surface does not include the vertical sides of the **tabletop**. 
 
• The playing surface yields a uniform bounce of about** 23cm** when a standard ball is dropped onto it from a height of** 30cm**. 
 
• The playing surface is matte surface and dark-colored.
 
• There is a white side line, **2cm wide,** along each** 2.74m** edge, and a white end line,** 2cm wide**, along each** 1.525m edge**. 
 
• The playing surface is divided into two equal courts by a vertical net parallel to the **end lines.**
 
• For doubles, each court is divided into two equal half courts by a white center line, **3mm wide**, running parallel with the sidelines.
 
• The center line forms part of each **right half-court**.

questions.question: Sultan Mahmud of Ghazni, raided which famous Indian temple?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Somnath Temple, Gujarat.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahmud of Ghazni in 1025 AD attacked and looted the Somnath Mandir located in Prabhas Patan near Veraval in Saurashtra** on the western coast of Gujarat.
 
• Mahmud of Ghazni was the** ruler of Afghanistan**.
 
• The plundered Somnath Mandir was rebuilt by the** Paramara king Bhoja **of Malwa and the **Solanki king Bhimdev I **of Anhilwara between 1026 and 1042 AD.
 
• Mahmud of Ghazni was a Turkish conqueror who attacked India 17 times between 1000 to 1027 AD.
 
• The biggest invasion of Mahmud of Ghazni was in **1025 AD **wherein he invaded the Somnath temple in Gujarat.
 
• In all his **17 invasions**, a number of dynasties were conquered by him.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Temple
 Location
 Brief Description
 
 
 
 

 Somnath Temple
 Gujarat, India
 One of the twelve Jyotirlinga shrines of Lord Shiva, Somnath Temple is a highly revered pilgrimage site for Hindus. This historical temple is said to have been destroyed and rebuilt several times, with the present temple constructed in the Chalukya style of architecture and completed in 1951.
 
 

 Jagannath Puri Temple
 Odisha, India
 This temple is a famous and sacred Hindu pilgrimage site dedicated to Lord Jagannath, a form of Lord Vishnu. The temple is known for its annual Rath Yatra, or chariot festival, in which the three main temple deities are hauled on huge and elaborately decorated temple cars. The current temple structure was built in the 12th century.
 
 

 Yamunotri Temple
 Uttarakhand, India
 Yamunotri Temple is the first stop in the Char Dham Yatra (pilgrimage) of Uttarakhand, dedicated to Goddess Yamuna. It's situated in the Western region of Garhwal Himalayas at an altitude of 3293 meters. The shrine is surrounded by undulating peaks and thermal springs, offering stunning scenic beauty.
 
 

 Lingaraj Temple
 Odisha, India
 This ancient temple, dedicated to Harihara, a form of Shiva and Vishnu, is one of the oldest temples in Bhubaneswar, Odisha. The temple dates back to the 11th century and is a masterpiece of the Orissan style of architecture. The 54.8-meter high central tower dominates the landscape.

questions.question: In June 2022, Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has released a report titled _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Payments Vision 2025**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Payment Vision 2025 document.

 
 
• On July 17, 2022, the Reserve Bank of India published its vision for 'Architecture of Digital Finance' in a document for Payment Systems. 
 
• This is known as the Payment Vision 2025 document. 
 
• The core theme of the Payments Vision 2025 is '**E-Payments for Everyone, Everywhere, Everytime' (4Es)**.
 
• It aims to provide every user with safe, secure, fast, convenient, accessible, and affordable e-payment options.
 
 
 
• Payments Vision 2025 has been prepared by considering the guidance from the** Board for Regulation and Supervision of Payment and Settlement Systems** of the RBI.
 
• It builds on the initiatives of Payments** Vision 2019-21**.
 
• The Payments Vision 2025 document is presented across the five anchor goalposts of I**ntegrity, Inclusion, Innovation, Institutionalisation and Internationalisation**.
 
• **Promoting digital payments:** The RBI is promoting the use of digital payments through a number of initiatives, such as the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) and the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).
 
• **Regulating the payments ecosystem:** The RBI is also working to regulate the payments ecosystem to ensure that it is safe and secure.
 
• **Building capacity:** The RBI is working to build capacity in the payments ecosystem by training financial institutions and businesses on how to use digital payments.

questions.question: Lucknow Pact was signed between __________.

options.text: the Muslim League and Mahatma Gandhi
the Indian National Congress and Arya Samaj
the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League
the Indian National Congress and Sayyid Ahmed Khan

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** The Lucknow Pact** was an agreement reached by the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League in the year 1916 in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, India.
 
• This pact marked a significant milestone in the Indian freedom struggle, as it was one of the first instances of Hindu-Muslim unity against British rule.
 
• The two major political parties of India at that time, the Indian National Congress and the All India Muslim League, had divergent views and goals. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The key features of the Lucknow Pact were as follows:
 
• **Provincial Autonomy: **The pact advocated for greater provincial autonomy, which was a shift from the demand for mere administrative reforms.
 
• **Separate Electorates:** One of the significant concessions made by the Indian National Congress was the acceptance of separate electorates for Muslims. 
 
• **Weightage to Minorities**: The pact also provided for weightage for minority communities in representative institutions. 
 
• **Unaltered Representation in Provinces: **The pact provided for an unchanged representation of Muslims in the provinces where they were in minority, but their representation could be increased in provinces where they were in majority.

questions.question:
Identify the Indian music personality.

Under him the shehnai came out of its ceremonial context and began to be acknowledged as a classical music instrument.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Ustad Bismillah Khan**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ustad Bismillah Khan** was a **shehnai virtuoso from India.**
 
• He brought the shehnai, a wind instrument traditionally played in ceremonies, into the concert stage, and was instrumental in elevating its status to that of a classical instrument.
 
• He was awarded India's highest civilian honor,** the Bharat Ratna, in 2001.**

**​** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alla Rakha: **

 
 
• Ustad Alla Rakha was an internationally acclaimed Indian tabla player.
 
• He was renowned for his virtuoso accompaniment and solo performances.
 
• He popularized Indian percussion music worldwide, often performing with renowned sitar player Pandit Ravi Shankar.
 
 
 
• **Pandit Ram Narayan: **
 
 
• Pandit Ram Narayan is an internationally acclaimed Indian musician, considered by many as the finest sarangi player.
 
• He is credited with bringing the sarangi, a bowed, short-necked string instrument, into the solo limelight from its traditional role as an accompanying instrument in Indian classical music.
 
 
 
• **Ustad Bundu Khan: **
 
 
• Ustad Bundu Khan was a prominent sarangi player from the traditional Indian subcontinent.
 
• He was known for his unique style and contributions to Indian classical music.
 
• He served at the court of the princely state of Jodhpur and later migrated to Pakistan after the partition of India in 1947.

questions.question: An image which can be obtained on a screen is called a ____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**real image**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In optics, a **real image** is an image that is formed when rays converge at a specific point.
 
• They can be projected onto a screen or a photographic film.
 
• Real images can be produced by concave mirrors and converging** lenses, assuming the object is placed further from the mirror or lens than the focal point, and this image is inverted.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vector Image:**

 
 
• This refers to a type of digital graphic that uses mathematical formulas to render its design, instead of using pixel data like raster images.
 
• Because of this, vector images can be scaled to any size without loss of resolution. 
 
 
 
• **Virtual Image:**
 
 
• In the field of optics, a virtual image is an image formed when the outgoing rays from a point on the object always diverge.
 
• The image appears to be located at the point of apparent divergence.
 
• Because the rays never really converge, a virtual image cannot be projected onto a screen.
 
• Examples of virtual images include the image seen in a single plane mirror, the image seen through a magnifying glass, or the image seen in a camera viewfinder.
 
 
 
• **Spectral Image: **
 
 
• A spectral image is an image whose pixels contain information from across the electromagnetic spectrum.
 
• These images are captured by spectral imaging techniques which capture the entire spectrum in each pixel.
 
• These images are used for various purposes like remote sensing, astrophysics, etc.

questions.question: In biology, the term "IVF" stands for __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** In vitro fertilization**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In Vitro Fertilization (IVF)** is a type of assisted reproductive technology (ART) used to help individuals or couples conceive a child.
 
• The term** "in vitro"** is a Latin term meaning** "in glass,"** referring to the test tubes used in laboratories, although the actual process now uses more advanced technology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Here is a basic outline of the IVF process:
 
• **Ovarian stimulation and monitoring: **
 
 
• The woman is given hormonal medications to stimulate the ovaries to produce multiple eggs instead of the single egg typically released during a menstrual cycle.
 
• Regular ultrasound and blood tests are performed to monitor the development of the follicles (fluid-filled ovarian sacs that contain the eggs).
 
 
 
• **Egg retrieval: **
 
 
• Once the eggs mature, a medical procedure known as follicular aspiration is performed to retrieve them.
 
• A thin needle is inserted through the vagina and into the ovary under ultrasound guidance, and the fluid in the follicles is aspirated.
 
 
 
• **Insemination and Fertilization: **
 
 
• The eggs are combined with sperm in a petri dish and incubated overnight. If traditional IVF doesn't seem promising, a single sperm may be injected directly into an egg, a process known as intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI).
 
 
 
• **Embryo culture: **
 
 
• The fertilized eggs (now embryos) are monitored for growth.
 
• The goal is to grow these embryos for about five days until they reach a stage called the blastocyst stage.
 
 
 
• **Embryo transfer: **
 
 
• Once the embryos are ready, one or more are transferred into the woman's uterus through the cervix using a thin catheter.
 
• If an embryo implants in the lining of the uterus and grows, a pregnancy results.

questions.question: The leaves have a green pigment called __________, which helps leaves to capture the energy from the sunlight.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chlorophyll**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chlorophyll **is a **green pigment found in the chloroplasts of plants, algae**, and s**ome bacteria.**
 
• It's crucial for photosynthesis, a process by which** light energy** is converted into **chemical energy**.
 
• **Chlorophyll **absorbs light most efficiently in the blue and red portions of the **electromagnetic spectrum, but poorly in the green portions, which it reflects, making the plant appear green.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cladophyll:**

 
 
• A **cladophyll** is a type of **leaf-like structure** that is actually a **stem**.
 
• These structures carry out **photosynthesis** and often resemble and function like leaves.
 
• **The primary function **of the **cladophyll **is not **pigment-based** but to **carry out photosynthesis and occasionally store water**.
 
• An example of a plant with cladophylls is the **asparagus.**
 
 
 
• **Xanthophyll:**
 
 
• **Xanthophyll **is a** yellow pigment** and is a type of accessory pigment, or **secondary pigment, found in the chloroplasts of plants.**
 
• It absorbs **light** in a** wavelength range** that **chlorophyll **cannot, and helps protect the plant from the harmful effects of excessive light energy.
 
 
 
• **Cytoplasm:**
 
 
• **The cytoplasm** is a component of the cell that is present within the cell membrane but outside the nucleus.
 
• It's a jelly-like substance where many metabolic reactions occur and contains various organelles such as mitochondria, ribosomes, etc.
 
• Although it's vital for the cell's functioning, it doesn't contain pigments or directly participate in **photosynthesis**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Karnataka: **
 
• This state is located in the **southwestern region of India.**
 
• **Karnataka** is known for various forms of **music, dance, drama, and visual arts.**
 
• **Yakshagana,** a theater form that combines** dance, music, dialogue, costume, make-up, and stage techniques with a unique style and form, is particularly popular.**
 
• **The Bhoota Kola** ritual dance is a spirit worship dance performed mainly in the **coastal districts of the state.**
 
• In this** traditional ritual, performers dress up as spirits and gods, enacting scenes and stories from local folklore and mythology**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Andhra Pradesh:**

 
 
• It is Located in the southeastern part of the country,** Andhra Pradesh** has a rich cultural history and is known for various forms of dance and music.
 
• The classical dance form of Kuchipudi originated in this state.
 
• There are also various folk and tribal dances such as **Butta Bommalu, Tappeta Gullu, and Dhimsa.**
 
 
 
• **Tamil Nadu:**
 
 
• It is Situated in the **southernmost part of India, Tamil Nadu** is known for its distinct **culture and heritage.**
 
• **Bharatanatyam**, one of the most popular and respected dance forms of India, originated here.
 
• The state is also known for its music, literature, and various forms of traditional and folk dances like **Karakattam, Kummi, and Mayil Attam.**
 
 
 
• **Kerala: **
 
 
• This **southwestern state** is known for its **unique dance forms and cultural rituals**.
 
• **Kathakali, **a highly stylized** classical Indian dance-drama, and Mohiniyattam,** a classical dance form that represents a dance of an enchantress, are two major classical dance forms from Kerala.
 
• **Theyyam** and **Thirayattam** are popular ritualistic folk arts performed in the **northern part of the state.**

questions.question: As the river enters the plain it get twists and turns forming large bends known as ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is meanders.

 
• Meanders:
 
• Meanders are bends in a waterway or river.
 
• They form when moving water in a stream erodes the outer banks and widens its valley, and the inner part of the river has less energy and deposits what it is carrying.
 
• Over time, the meanders become more exaggerated.
 
• Ox-bow:
 
• An oxbow is a U-shaped body of water that forms when a wide meander from the main stem of a river is cut off, creating a free-standing body of water.
 
• This landform is named for its distinctive curved shape, which is similar to the yoke used to harness oxen.
 
• Levees:
 
• Levees are natural embankments which are built up along the edges of a river channel.
 
• During flood stages, water deposits sediment on the river banks, creating levees.
 
• They act as barriers against floodwater and are also often reinforced by humans in areas prone to flooding.
 
• Stack:
 
• A stack is a geological landform consisting of a steep and often vertical column or columns of rock in the sea near a coast, formed by wave erosion.
 
• Stacks are formed over time by wind and water, processes of coastal geomorphology.

questions.question: "Arthashastra" was written by ___________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chanakya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Arthashastra

 
 
• The Arthashastra is one of the earliest works of political realism to have been written, along with Sun Tzu's The Art of War and Machiavelli's The Prince.
 
• The 'Arthashastra' is a treasure of Political Philosophy. Hence, Option 3 is correct.
 
• It is considered the most comprehensive treatise on statecraft of classical times.
 
• The first-ever book written on Practice of Management, this treatise is also about foreign policy, administration, economic reforms, policies, and war.
 
• It is a primeval Indian discourse on statecraft, economic policy, and military strategy. 
 
• It is written in Sanskrit. 
 
• Kautilya's Arthasashtra was composed between the 3rd to 2nd Century B.C.
 
• It is mainly a work on the art of government.
 
• In his view, for the smooth functioning of administration and the welfare of the people, the king had to be acquainted with the four Vedas and four sciences of government (Anvikashaki, Trai, Varta, and Dandniti). 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

 
• Kautilya's administrative and judicial structure was hierarchical.
 
• He emphasized the principle of equity.
 
• He believed that law was an imperial command enforced by sanctions.
 
• He was both a thinker and statesman.
 
• He contributed to the formulation of some general principles capable of universal application and effectiveness in all times and ages.
 
• Arthsashtra sets the conceptual groundwork for making India the first welfare state.
 
• In Indian theory, State was usually thought to cover seven elements:
 
 
• The king
 
• The ministers
 
• The populace
 
• The fort
 
• The treasury
 
• The army
 
• The ally

questions.question: For a bank, the main liability is the __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**deposits**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The key business of the banks is to accept different types of deposits from the public and then lend these funds to the borrowers.
 
 
• This is called Financial intermediation.
 
 
 
• In terms of the banks, the deposits represent the “liabilities” of the banks while loans advanced and investments made by banks represent their “assets”.
 
• The deposit itself is a liability owed by the bank to the depositor.
 
• Bank deposits refer to this liability rather than to the actual funds that have been deposited.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• High Powered Money:

 
 
• The total liability of the monetary authority of the country, RBI, is called the monetary base or high-powered money.
 
• It consists of currency (notes and coins in circulation with the public and vault cash of commercial banks) and deposits held by the Government of India and commercial banks with RBI.
 
 
 
• If a member of the public produces a currency note to RBI the latter must pay her value equal to the figure printed on the note. Similarly, the deposits are also refundable by RBI on-demand from deposit-holders.
 
• These items are claims which the general public, government, or banks have on RBI and hence are considered to be the liability of RBI. RBI acquires assets against these liabilities.
 
• This can be understood by an example. Suppose RBI purchases gold or dollars worth Rs 5. It pays for the gold or foreign exchange by issuing currency to the seller. The currency in circulation in the economy thus goes up by Rs 5, an item that shows up on the liability side of the balance sheet. The value of the acquired assets, also equal to Rs 5, is entered under the appropriate head on the Assets side.
 
• Similarly, RBI acquires debt bonds or securities issued by the government and pays the government by issuing currency in return. It issues loans to commercial banks in a similar fashion.
 
• However, the most important role of RBI is as the controller of money supply and credit creation in the economy.
 
• RBI is the independent authority for conducting monetary policy in the best interests of the economy – it increases or decreases the supply of high-powered money in the economy and creates incentives or disincentives for the commercial banks to give loans or credits to investors.

questions.question: Which Mughal Emperor has attempted to vandalise the Kailash Temple at Ellora?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aurangzeb**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Mughal emperor who is often attributed with attempts to vandalise the Kailash Temple at Ellora is:**
 
• **Aurangzeb**
 
 
• Aurangzeb, whose full name was **Abul Muzaffar Muhi-ud-Din Muhammad Aurangzeb, ruled the Mughal Empire from 1658 to 1707.**
 
• He is known for his strict adherence to **Islam and the implementation of Islamic laws during his reign.**
 
• Aurangzeb was known for his military campaigns and extended the Mughal empire to its **greatest extent**.
 
• However, his** religious policies are often blamed for causing resentment among his Hindu subjects, which included the destruction or desecration of Hindu temples.**
 
• Reports suggest that he attempted to vandalise the** Kailash Temple at Ellora, an example of his iconoclastic policies, although the temple survived largely intact.**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• **Kailasha Temple Ellora**

 
 
• ​__The Kailasha Temple is the largest of the rock-cut Hindu temples at the Ellora Caves, Maharashtra.
 
• It is considered one of the most remarkable cave temples in the world because of its size, architecture and sculptural treatment, and the climax of the rock-cut phase of Indian architecture.
 
• The Kailasa temple is the largest of the 34 Buddhist, Jain, and Hindu cave temples and monasteries known collectively as the Ellora Caves, ranging for over 2 kilometers along the sloping basalt cliff at the site.
 
• The temple architecture shows traces of Pallava and Chalukya styles.
 
• The temple contains a number of relief and free-standing sculptures on a grand scale equal to the architecture, though only traces remain of the paintings which originally decorated it.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**
